questions.text: Foreign exchange rate refers to:

options.label: a
options.text: the price of gold in terms of the domestic currency

options.label: b
options.text: the price of one unit of a foreign currency in terms of the domestic currency

options.label: c
options.text: the ratio of a country's exports to its imports

options.label: d
options.text: the rate of interest charged on foreign loans

questions.text: Under the flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by:

options.label: a
options.text: the central bank alone

options.label: b
options.text: the market forces of demand for and supply of foreign exchange

options.label: c
options.text: the government of the country

options.label: d
options.text: the World Bank

questions.text: Under the fixed exchange rate system, the exchange rate is officially fixed by:

options.label: a
options.text: the commercial banks

options.label: b
options.text: the market forces of demand and supply

options.label: c
options.text: the government / central bank

options.label: d
options.text: the exporters of the country

questions.text: Which of the following is a source of demand for foreign exchange?

options.label: a
options.text: Import of goods and services from abroad

options.label: b
options.text: Export of goods to other countries

options.label: c
options.text: Foreign tourists visiting India

options.label: d
options.text: Remittances received from Indians working abroad

questions.text: Which of the following is a source of supply of foreign exchange?

options.label: a
options.text: Import of machinery from abroad

options.label: b
options.text: Export of goods and services

options.label: c
options.text: Indian students paying fees to foreign universities

options.label: d
options.text: Indians buying shares of foreign companies

questions.text: A fall in the value of the domestic currency in terms of a foreign currency under the flexible exchange rate system is called:

options.label: a
options.text: depreciation

options.label: b
options.text: appreciation

options.label: c
options.text: devaluation

options.label: d
options.text: revaluation

questions.text: A deliberate reduction in the value of the domestic currency by the government under the fixed exchange rate system is called:

options.label: a
options.text: appreciation

options.label: b
options.text: depreciation

options.label: c
options.text: devaluation

options.label: d
options.text: revaluation

questions.text: A rise in the value of the domestic currency in terms of a foreign currency under the flexible exchange rate system is called:

options.label: a
options.text: devaluation

options.label: b
options.text: revaluation

options.label: c
options.text: appreciation

options.label: d
options.text: depreciation

questions.text: The demand curve for foreign exchange is:

options.label: a
options.text: a horizontal straight line

options.label: b
options.text: downward sloping from left to right

options.label: c
options.text: upward sloping from left to right

options.label: d
options.text: a vertical straight line

questions.text: The exchange rate system in which the rate is mainly determined by the market, but the central bank intervenes to limit sharp fluctuations, is called the:

options.label: a
options.text: managed floating exchange rate system

options.label: b
options.text: purely flexible exchange rate system

options.label: c
options.text: system of zero foreign trade

options.label: d
options.text: fixed exchange rate system

questions.text: In a flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate changes from ₹80 per $ to ₹84 per $. This means the rupee has:

options.label: a
options.text: appreciated

options.label: b
options.text: been revalued

options.label: c
options.text: been devalued

options.label: d
options.text: depreciated

questions.text: In a flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate changes from ₹84 per $ to ₹80 per $. This means the rupee has:

options.label: a
options.text: appreciated

options.label: b
options.text: depreciated

options.label: c
options.text: been revalued

options.label: d
options.text: been devalued

questions.text: The supply curve of foreign exchange slopes upward because a rise in the exchange rate:

options.label: a
options.text: reduces foreign investment in the country

options.label: b
options.text: makes domestic goods costlier for foreigners

options.label: c
options.text: makes imports cheaper for domestic buyers

options.label: d
options.text: makes domestic goods cheaper for foreigners, so exports increase

questions.text: The demand curve for foreign exchange slopes downward because a rise in the exchange rate:

options.label: a
options.text: makes domestic goods costlier for foreigners

options.label: b
options.text: makes imports cheaper, so the demand for foreign exchange rises

options.label: c
options.text: makes imports costlier, so the demand for foreign exchange falls

options.label: d
options.text: makes exports costlier for foreigners

questions.text: In a flexible exchange rate system, the equilibrium exchange rate is determined at the point where:

options.label: a
options.text: demand for foreign exchange is more than its supply

options.label: b
options.text: demand for foreign exchange equals supply of foreign exchange

options.label: c
options.text: the government announces the rate

options.label: d
options.text: exports of the country become zero

questions.text: If the exchange rate is above the equilibrium rate in a free market, there will be:

options.label: a
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

options.label: b
options.text: excess demand for foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

options.label: c
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will fall

options.label: d
options.text: no change in the rate

questions.text: If the exchange rate is below the equilibrium rate in a free market, there will be:

options.label: a
options.text: excess demand for foreign exchange, and the rate will fall

options.label: b
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will fall

options.label: c
options.text: excess supply of foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

options.label: d
options.text: excess demand for foreign exchange, and the rate will rise

questions.text: Depreciation of the domestic currency is likely to make the country's exports:

options.label: a
options.text: cheaper for foreigners, so exports decrease

options.label: b
options.text: costlier for foreigners, so exports decrease

options.label: c
options.text: unaffected

options.label: d
options.text: cheaper for foreigners, so exports increase

questions.text: Depreciation of the domestic currency is likely to make imports:

options.label: a
options.text: unaffected

options.label: b
options.text: costlier in domestic currency, so imports increase

options.label: c
options.text: cheaper in domestic currency, so imports increase

options.label: d
options.text: costlier in domestic currency, so imports decrease

questions.text: Appreciation of the domestic currency is likely to:

options.label: a
options.text: increase exports and reduce imports

options.label: b
options.text: have no effect on exports and imports

options.label: c
options.text: reduce exports and increase imports

options.label: d
options.text: increase both exports and imports

questions.text: In a flexible exchange rate system, if the demand for foreign exchange increases while its supply remains unchanged, the exchange rate will:

options.label: a
options.text: remain unchanged

options.label: b
options.text: fall, i.e. the domestic currency will appreciate

options.label: c
options.text: rise, i.e. the domestic currency will depreciate

options.label: d
options.text: fall, i.e. the domestic currency will depreciate

questions.text: In a flexible exchange rate system, if the supply of foreign exchange increases while its demand remains unchanged, the exchange rate will:

options.label: a
options.text: rise, i.e. the domestic currency will depreciate

options.label: b
options.text: remain unchanged

options.label: c
options.text: fall, i.e. the domestic currency will appreciate

options.label: d
options.text: rise, i.e. the domestic currency will appreciate

questions.text: Which of the following will shift the demand curve for foreign exchange to the right?

options.label: a
options.text: Increase in foreign tourists visiting the country

options.label: b
options.text: Increase in foreign investment in the country

options.label: c
options.text: Rise in domestic residents' preference for foreign goods

options.label: d
options.text: Rise in the country's exports

questions.text: Which of the following will shift the supply curve for foreign exchange to the right?

options.label: a
options.text: Indians investing more in foreign countries

options.label: b
options.text: Increase in foreign investment in India

options.label: c
options.text: More Indians travelling abroad

options.label: d
options.text: Increase in India's imports

questions.text: A deliberate increase in the value of the domestic currency by the government under the fixed exchange rate system is called:

options.label: a
options.text: appreciation

options.label: b
options.text: revaluation

options.label: c
options.text: depreciation

options.label: d
options.text: devaluation

questions.text: Which of the following is a merit of the flexible exchange rate system?

options.label: a
options.text: It requires constant government intervention

options.label: b
options.text: The exchange rate never changes

options.label: c
options.text: It ensures complete stability of the exchange rate

options.label: d
options.text: The government need not maintain large foreign exchange reserves

questions.text: Which of the following is a merit of the fixed exchange rate system?

options.label: a
options.text: It does not require any foreign exchange reserves

options.label: b
options.text: It adjusts automatically to market conditions

options.label: c
options.text: It is completely free from government control

options.label: d
options.text: It brings stability in the exchange rate, which encourages international trade

questions.text: Which of the following is a demerit of the fixed exchange rate system?

options.label: a
options.text: It requires the central bank to maintain large foreign exchange reserves

options.label: b
options.text: It removes the role of the government

options.label: c
options.text: It is determined only by market forces

options.label: d
options.text: The exchange rate fluctuates every day

questions.text: Which of the following is a demerit of the flexible exchange rate system?

options.label: a
options.text: It requires large foreign exchange reserves

options.label: b
options.text: Frequent fluctuations in the exchange rate create uncertainty in international trade

options.label: c
options.text: The government must fix the rate every day

options.label: d
options.text: The exchange rate is rigid and cannot change

questions.text:
Under the managed floating system, if the domestic currency is depreciating sharply, the central bank will usually:
(a) stop all imports (b) sell foreign currency from its reserves
(c) fix the exchange rate permanently (d) buy foreign currency from the market

options.label: a
options.text: stop all imports

options.label: b
options.text: sell foreign currency from its reserves

options.label: c
options.text: fix the exchange rate permanently

options.label: d
options.text: buy foreign currency from the market

questions.text:
Under the managed floating system, to prevent a sharp appreciation of the domestic currency, the central bank will usually:
(a) ban all exports (b) allow the rate to move freely without any action
(c) sell foreign currency from its reserves (d) buy foreign currency from the market

options.label: a
options.text: ban all exports

options.label: b
options.text: allow the rate to move freely without any action

options.label: c
options.text: sell foreign currency from its reserves

options.label: d
options.text: buy foreign currency from the market

options.label: c

options.text: ₹40,000 (no change)

questions.text:
Assertion (A): When the rupee depreciates, the demand for Indian exports tends to rise.

options.label: b
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: c
options.text: A is true, but R is false.

options.label: d
options.text: A is false, but R is true.

questions.text:

Reason (R): Under the flexible exchange rate system, the exchange rate is determined by market forces.

options.label: a

options.label: b
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

options.label: c

options.label: d
